restack-already-current-summary.description: sr restack reports branches it skipped as already stacked on their parent, instead of silently omitting them

context.text: Counts, not names, for already-current branches: names would flood sr sync -a over many stacks; the count alone makes the summary add up to sr log

sync-readable-output.description: sr sync output reads as a short report: quiet git plumbing, trunk delta, cleaned branches with reasons, restack summary

context.text: Quiet the git plumbing (fetch/merge/rebase/branch -D --quiet, captured rebase) and have sync state trunk delta, deletions with reasons, restack summary in its own words

Rebase output is captured, not forwarded: on a skipped conflict only the conflicted files are reported; on a paused conflict only CONFLICT lines print. git's hints prescribe raw git rebase --continue, which desyncs the graph
